neet_che_u03_t16_1.working: In o-nitrophenol, the -OH and -NO2 groups are adjacent, so they form an H-bond within the same molecule (a chelate ring). p-Nitrophenol, acetic acid dimers and ethanol all H-bond between molecules.

neet_che_u03_t16_2.working: Observed boiling points are H2O 373 K, HF about 293 K and NH3 about 240 K. Water forms more H-bonds per molecule (two H atoms and two lone pairs), so the order is H2O > HF > NH3.

neet_che_u03_t16_3.working: In ice, H-bonding fixes each molecule in a tetrahedral open cage with empty spaces. This makes ice less dense than liquid water, so it floats.

neet_che_u03_t16_4.working: o-Nitrophenol is the steam-volatile isomer, because intramolecular H-bonding stops it associating with other molecules. p-Nitrophenol is associated through intermolecular H-bonds and is not steam volatile. So A is false and R is true.

neet_che_u03_t16_5.working: Statement I is wrong: H-bond strength is F-H···F > O-H···O > N-H···N. Statement II is wrong: intramolecular H-bonding in salicylaldehyde lowers its boiling point and water solubility. Both statements are incorrect.
